title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

reading.body:
This is a case of an automated identification system's output being acted on as though it were a confirmed fact. A license plate reading camera flagged a stolen plate, and that alert travelled into a live armed response: multiple patrol cars, a helicopter, guns drawn and handcuffs, before anyone established that the vehicle in front of them was the wrong car. The failure sits at the handoff between the camera alert and the officers in the field, where a database match was treated as an identification of the people inside the car.

The gap that allowed it is visible in the reporting itself. Deputies could not read the license plate, and rather than resolving that before escalating, they called for backup and continued. A visual confirmation of the plate, or any check that the alert matched the vehicle actually present, would have caught the error at the point where it was still cheap to catch. The system had flagged a plate, not a car and not two 19 year olds.

What is not established is whether the deputy threatened to shoot, which is the account of the two men, and whether any procedure was violated, which the sheriff's office has said supervisors will review through body worn camera footage. No charges were filed, and the men plan to pursue a formal complaint. A review is not a finding, and a complaint is not a determination.

reports.title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

summary:
Harris County sheriff's deputies in Cypress, Texas, mistook two men, both 19, Anthony and Julian, for car thieves on Aug. 3. Deputies surrounded Anthony's Camaro with at least five patrol cars and a helicopter, pointed guns, handcuffed them, and one deputy threatened to shoot, according to the men. The deputies thought the car was a stolen Camaro linked to aggravated robberies after license plate reading cameras detected a stolen plate. They could not read the license plate, called backup, then realized it was the wrong car.

The men are not facing charges, and deputies explained the mistake to them. Anthony's mother, Leslie, wants accountability and plans to hire an attorney. The sheriff's office says supervisors will review body worn camera footage to check whether procedures were followed. A spokesperson said the men were given information about filing a formal complaint with internal affairs, and both plan to do so.
title_en: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say
